checks.label: Medium 2 has a greater index of refraction than medium 1. This means that the speed of light is less in medium 2 than in medium 1: each marcher walks 1.333 times slower once in the water, and the row, square to the ray before, stands square to the bent ray after, turned towards the normal, for angles from 5° to 75°; square on it does not turn

The refractive index is the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction: for every angle from 3° to 80°, sin i ÷ sin r is 1.333 into water and 1.50 into glass, and Snell's law screen ends on 40°, 28.8° and 1.333 (sin 40° = 0.643, sin r = 0.482)
Refractive index is the velocity of light in empty space divided by its velocity in a substance: 3.00 × 10⁸ ÷ 1.333 = 2.25 × 10⁸ m/s in water, and the glass block's 3.00 × 10⁸ ÷ 2.00 × 10⁸ = 1.50

The critical angle is reached when the angle of refraction reaches 90 degrees: from water into air that is 48.6° (sin c = 1 ÷ 1.333 = 0.750), where the bent ray lies along the surface; past it no ray leaves and all of it reflects; from glass it is 41.8°

Traced straight back, the eye's rays from a coin 1.2 m down meet 0.90 m down when the eye is straight above (1.2 ÷ 1.333), and 0.45 m down for a coin 0.60 m down; every ray obeys the law at the surface, from every eye position the lines back meet above the coin, and the rod aimed there passes over it

A higher index turns light further: through the prism violet is turned most and red least; inside a 45° prism the light meets the long face at 45°, past glass's 41.8° critical angle, so all of it reflects through 90°, but short of water's 48.6°, so in water it gets out

Each typed answer and slip is worked from the lesson's figures: 3.00 ÷ 2.00 = 1.50 (0.67, 1.33); sin r = 0.766 ÷ 1.50 gives 30.7° (33.3, 59.3, 50); 0.60 ÷ 1.333 = 0.45 m (0.80, 0.60); sin c = 1 ÷ 1.50 gives 41.8° (48.6, 48.2); 1.333 × 0.5 ÷ 1.50 = 0.444 gives 26.4° (19.5, 34.2); each answer as printed is graded right and each slip wrong, and each solved picture prints its answer
Before Check nothing gives the answer away: no typed answer is drawn, no ray or seeming coin is drawn in the tank, the square-on ray stops at the surface, and nothing leaves the water prism
Every demonstration settles within 5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; each switch's motion and every answer's motion settle within 3 s
